verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              युगक्षयात्परिक्षीणे धर्मे लोके च भारत । दस्युभिः पीड्यमाने च कथं स्थेयं पितामह ॥१॥
verses.english: Brahmanas well read in the subjects of enquiry speak of the two feet as Spiritual, the act of walking as Elemental and Vishnu as Accidental.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि नीतिमापत्सु भारत । उत्सृज्यापि घृणां काले यथा वर्तेत भूमिपः ॥२॥
verses.english: The lower duct is Spiritual; its function of throwing out the excreta is Elemental, and Mitra (Surya) is the Accidental.

verses.sanskrit: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । भारद्वाजस्य संवादं राज्ञः शत्रुजयस्य च ॥३॥
verses.english: The organ of generation is called Spiritual. Its agreeable function is called Elemental and Prajapati is its Accidental.

verses.sanskrit: राजा शत्रुजयो नाम सौवीरेषु महारथः । भारद्वाजमुपागम्य पप्रच्छार्थविनिश्चयम् ॥४॥
verses.english: The hands are Spiritual; their function as represented by acts is Elemental; and Indra is the Accident of those limbs.

verses.sanskrit: अलब्धस्य कथं लिप्सा लब्धं केन विवर्धते । वर्धितं पाल्यते केन पालितं प्रणयेत्कथम् ॥५॥
तस्मै विनिश्चितार्थाय परिपृष्टोऽर्थनिश्चयम् । उवाच ब्राह्मणो वाक्यमिदं हेतुमदुत्तमम् ॥६॥
नित्यमुद्यतदण्डः स्यान्नित्यं विवृतपौरुषः । अच्छिद्रश्छिद्रदर्शी च परेषां विवरानुगः ॥७॥
नित्यमुद्यतदण्डस्य भृशमुद्विजते नरः । तस्मात्सर्वाणि भूतानि दण्डेनैव प्रसाधयेत् ॥८॥
एवं दण्डं प्रशंसन्ति पण्डितास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः । तस्माच्चतुष्टये तस्मिन्प्रधानो दण्ड उच्यते ॥९॥
छिन्नमूले त्वधिष्ठाने सर्वेषां जीवनं हतम् । कथ हि शाखास्तिष्ठेयुश्छिन्नमूले वनस्पतौ ॥१०॥
मूलमेवादितश्छिन्द्यात्परपक्षस्य पण्डितः । ततः सहायान् पक्षं च मूलमेवानुसाधयेत् ॥११॥
सुमन्त्रितं सुविक्रान्तं सुयुद्धं सुपलायितम् । आपदास्पदकाले तु कुर्वीत न विचारयेत् ॥१२॥
वाङ्मात्रेण विनीतः स्याद्धृदयेन यथा क्षुरः । श्लक्ष्णपूर्वाभिभाषी च कामक्रोधौ विवर्जयेत् ॥१३॥
सपत्नसहिते कार्ये कृत्वा सन्धिं न विश्वसेत् । अपक्रामेत् ततः शीघं कृतकार्यो विचक्षणः ॥१४॥
शत्रु च मित्ररूपेण सान्त्वेनैवाभिसान्त्वयेत् । नित्यशश्नोद्विजेत्तस्माद्गृहात्सर्पयुतादिव ॥१५॥
यस्य बुद्धिः परिभवेत्तमतीतेन सान्त्वयेत् । अनागतेन दुष्प्रज्ञं प्रत्युत्पन्नेन पण्डितम् ॥१६॥
अञ्जलिं शपथं सान्त्वं प्रणम्य शिरसा वदेत् । अश्रुप्रमार्जनं चैव कर्तव्यं भूतिमिच्छता ॥१७॥
वहेदमित्रं स्कन्धेन यावत्कालस्य पर्ययः । प्राप्तकालं तु विज्ञाय भिन्द्याद्घटमिवाश्मनि ॥१८॥
मुहूर्तमपि राजेन्द्र तिन्दुकालातवज्ज्वलेत् । न तुषाग्निरिवानर्चिर्धूमायेत चिरं नरः ॥१९॥
verses.english: The characteristics of the quality of Darkness are pride of personal beauty, assertion of supremacy, war, disinclination to give, absence of mercy, enjoyment and enduring of happiness and misery, pleasure in speaking ill of others, habit of quarrelling, pride, discourtesy, anxiety, hostilities, sorrow, appropriation of others' properties, shamelessness, crookedness, disunion, roughness, lust, anger, pride, assertion of superiority, malice and calumny. These originate from the quality of Darkness. I shall now tell you of qualities which originate Ignorance.

verses.sanskrit: नानार्थिकोऽर्थसम्बन्धं कृतघ्नेन समाचरेत् । अर्थी तु शक्यते भोक्तुं कृतकार्योऽवमन्यते । तस्मात्सर्वाणि कार्याणि सावशेषाणि कारयेत् ॥२०॥
कोकिलस्य वराहस्य मेरोः शून्यस्य वेश्मनः । नटस्य भक्तिमित्रस्य यच्छ्रेचस्तत्समाचरेत् ॥२१॥
verses.english: Besides these, the other marks of Ignorance are greediness for food, ceaseless appetite for both food and drink, taking pleasure in scents and dresses and sports and beds and seats and sleep during the day and calumny and all sorts of acts proceeding from carelessness, taking pleasure, in dancing and instrumental and vocal music, and aversion for every sort of religion. These, indeed, are the characteristics of Ignorance.

verses.sanskrit: उत्थायोत्थाय गच्छेत नित्ययुक्तो रिपोर्गृहान् । कुशलं चास्य पृच्छेत यद्यप्यकुशलं भवेत् ॥२२॥
verses.english: The king should, always, with careful application, go to the houses of his enemies, and even if calamities overtake them, ask them about their well-being.

verses.sanskrit: नालसाः प्राप्नुवन्त्यर्थान्न क्लीबा नाभिमानिनः । न च लोकरवाद्भीता न वै शश्वत्प्रतीक्षिणः ॥२३॥
verses.english: Those who are idle never acquire ricnes; nor those who are shorn of manliness and exertion; nor those who are vain; nor those who fear unpopularity; nor those who arc always dilatory.

verses.sanskrit: नात्मच्छिद्रं रिपुर्विद्याद्विहाच्छिद्रं परस्य तु । गूहेत्कूर्म इवाङ्गानि रक्षेद्विवरमात्मनः ॥२४॥
verses.english: The king should act in such way that his foe may not see his shortcomings. He should, however, himself notice the weak points of his enemy. He should imitate the tortoise which conceals its limbs. He should always keep hidden his own holes.

verses.sanskrit: बकवच्चिन्तयेदर्थान् सिंहतच्च पराक्रमेत् । वृकवच्चावलुम्पेत शरवच्च विनिष्पतेत् ॥२५॥
verses.english: He should think of all financial matters like a crane. He should show his prowess like a lion. He should lie in ambush like a wolf and attack and pierce his foes like an arrow.

verses.sanskrit: पानमक्षास्तथा नार्यो मृगया गीतवादितम् । एतानि युक्त्या सेवेत प्रसंगो ह्यत्र दोषवान् ॥२६॥
verses.english: He should be careful in his enjoyments regarding drink, dice, women, hunting, and music. Addiction to these produces evil.

verses.sanskrit: कुर्यात्तृणमयं चापं शयीत मृगशायिकाम् । अन्धः स्यादन्धवेलायां बाधिर्यमपि संश्रयेत् ॥२७॥
verses.english: He should make his bow of bamboos; he should sleep like the deer; he should be blind when it is necessary for him to be so, or he should even be deaf when it is necessary to be deaf.

verses.sanskrit: देशकालौ समासाद्य विक्रमेत विचक्षणः । देशकालव्यतीतो हि विक्रमो निष्फलो भवेत् ॥२८॥
verses.english: The wise king should display his prowess, considering time and place. If these are not favourable, prowess becomes useless.

verses.sanskrit: कालाकालौ सम्प्रधार्य बलाबलमथात्मनः । परस्य च बलं ज्ञात्वा तत्रात्मानं नियोजयेत् ॥२९॥
verses.english: Noting the opportune and inopportune moment, reflecting upon his own strength by comparing it with that of the enemy, the king should take up his work.

verses.sanskrit: दण्डेनोपनतं शत्रुं यो राजा न नियच्छति । स मृत्युमुपगृह्णाति गर्भमश्वतरी यथा ॥३०॥
verses.english: That king who does not crush down an enemy by military force, provides for his own death like the crab when she conceives.

verses.sanskrit: सुपुष्पितः स्यादफलः फलवान् स्याद्दुरारुहः । आमः स्यात्पक्वसंकाशो न च शीर्येत कस्यचित् ॥३१॥
verses.english: The king should show blossoms but not fruits. When showing fruits he should be difficult of climbing; and though unripe he should seem to be ripe. If he acts thus he would succeed in upholding himself against all enemies. then put man

verses.sanskrit: आशां कालवतीं कुर्यात्तां च विघ्न योजयेत् । विघ्नं निमित्ततो ब्रूयान्निमित्तं चापि हेतुतः ॥३२॥
verses.english: The king should first strengthen the hopes (of the suitors). He should impediments in the way of the fulfilment of those hopes. He should say that those impediments are merely due to time. He should next represent that those occasions are really the outcome of weighty causes.

verses.sanskrit: भीतवत्संविधातव्यं यावद्भयमनागतम् । आगतं तु भयं दृष्ट्वा प्रहर्तव्यमभीतवत् ॥३३॥
verses.english: As long as the cause of fear does not actually arrive, the king should make all his arrangements like a person filled with fear. When, however, the cause of fear arrives, he should smite fearlessly.

verses.sanskrit: न संशयमनारुह्य नरो भद्राणि पश्यति । संशयं पुनरारुह्य यदि जीवति पश्यति ॥३४॥
verses.english: No can derive benefit without incurring danger. If, again, he succeeds in preserving his life in the midst of danger's he is sure to acquire great benefits.

verses.sanskrit: अनागतं विजानीयाद्यच्छेद्भयमुपस्थितम् । पुनर्वृद्धिभयात्किंचिदनिवृत्तं निशामयेत् ॥३५॥
verses.english: A king should determine all future dangers; when they are present, he should conquer them; and lest they may grow again, he should, even after conquering them, consider them, as unconquered.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्युपस्थितकालस्य सुखस्य परिवर्जनम् । अनागतसुखाशा च नैव बुद्धिमतां नयः ॥३६॥
verses.english: The relinquishing of present happiness and the pursuit of the future one, is never the policy of an intelligent person.

verses.sanskrit: योऽरिणा सह संधाय सुखं स्वपिति विश्वसन् । स वृक्षाग्रे प्रसुप्तो वा पतितः प्रतिबुद्ध्यते ॥३७॥
verses.english: That king who having made peace with an enemy sleeps happily and confidently is lįke a man who sleeping on the top of a iree awakes after a fall,

verses.sanskrit: कर्मणा येन तेनैव मृदुना दारुणेन च । उद्धरेद्दीनमात्मानं समर्थो धर्ममाचरेत् ॥३८॥
verses.english: When one is in distress, he should raise himself by any means in his power. mild or stern; and after such advancement, he should, if able, practise virtue.

verses.sanskrit: ये सपत्नाः सपत्नानां सर्वांस्तानुपसेवयेत् । आत्मनश्चापि बोद्धव्याचारा विनिहताः परैः ॥३९॥
verses.english: The king should always honour the enemies of his foes. He should consider his own spies as agents employed by his enemies,

verses.sanskrit: चारस्त्वविदितः कार्य आत्मनोऽथ परस्य च । पाषण्डांस्तापसादींश्च परराष्ट्रे प्रवेशयेत् ॥४०॥
verses.english: The king should see that his own spies are not made out by his enemy. He should appoint atheists and ascetics as spies and despatch them to kingdom of his enemies. Sinful thieves, who violate the laws of virtue and who are thorns with every person, enter gardens and places of amusement and houses set up for giving drinking water to thirsty travellers and public restaurants and drinking spots and houses of ill fame and Tirthas and public assemblies. These should be recognised and arrested and suppressed.

verses.sanskrit: उद्यानेषु विहारेषु प्रपास्वावसथेषु च । पानागारे प्रवेशेषु तीर्थेषु च सभासु च ॥४१॥
धर्माभिचारिणः पापाश्चौरा लोकस्य कण्टकाः । समागच्छन्ति तान्बुद्ध्वा नियच्छेच्छमयीत च ॥४२॥
न विश्वसेदविश्वस्ते विश्वस्ते नातिविश्वसेत् । विश्वासाद्भयमभ्येति नापरीक्ष्य च विश्वसेद् ॥४३॥
verses.english: The king should not confide in an unworthy person; nor should he over confide in a person who is worthy of trust. Danger originates from confidence. Confidence should never be placed without previous examination.

verses.sanskrit: विश्वासयित्वा तु परं तत्त्वभूतेन हेतुना । अथास्य प्रहरेत्काले किंचिद्विचलिते पदे ॥४४॥
verses.english: Having by ostensible created confidence in the enemy, the king should strike him when he makes a mistake. reasons

verses.sanskrit: अशङ्क्यमपि शङ्केत नित्यं शङ्केत शङ्कितात् । भयं ह्यशङ्किताज्जातं समूलमपि कृन्तति ॥४५॥
verses.english: The king should fear him from whom there is no fear; he should also always fear them who should be feared. Fear rising from a person who is not feared, may bring on total extermination.

verses.sanskrit: अवधानेन मौनेन काषायेण जटाजिनैः । विश्वासयित्वा द्वेष्टारमवलुम्पेद्यथा वृकः ॥४६॥
verses.english: By devotion to religious pursuits, by taciturnity, by assuming the orange grab of monks, and wearing matted locks skins, one should create confidence in his enemy, and then, when the time comes, should pounce upon him like the wolf.

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रो वा यदि वा भ्राता पिता वा यदि वा सुहृत् । अर्थस्य विघ्नं कुर्वाणा हन्तव्या भूतिमिच्छता ॥४७॥
verses.english: A king seeking prosperity should not hesitate to kill son or brother or father or friend, if any of these seek to thwart his objects.

verses.sanskrit: गुरोरप्यवलिप्तस्य कार्याकार्यमजानतः । उत्पथं प्रतिपन्नस्य दण्डो भवति शासनम् ॥४८॥
verses.english: The very preceptor, if he is haughty, ignorant of what should be done and what should not, and an impious person, should be restrained by Punishment.

verses.sanskrit: अभ्युत्थानाभिवादाभ्यां सम्प्रदानेन केनचित् । प्रतिपुष्पकलाघाती तीक्ष्णतुण्ड इव द्विजः ॥४९॥
verses.english: As sharp-stinged insects cut off all the flowers and fruits of the trees on which they sit, the king should, after having created confidence in his enemies by honours, salutations and gifts, go against him and deprive him of everything.

verses.sanskrit: नाच्छित्त्वा परमर्माणि नाकृत्वा कर्म दारुणम् । नाहत्वा मत्स्यधातीव प्राप्नोति महतीं श्रियम् ॥५०॥
verses.english: Without cutting the very vitals of others, without killing living creatures like fishermen, one cannot win great prosperity.

verses.sanskrit: नास्ति जात्या रिपुर्नाम मित्रं वापि न विद्यते । सामर्थ्ययोगाज्जायन्ते मित्राणि रिपवस्तथा ॥५१॥
verses.english: There is no separate order of creatures called enemies or friends. Persons become friends or enemies according to the trend of circumstances.

verses.sanskrit: अमित्रं नैव मुञ्चेत वदन्तं करुणान्यपि । दुःखं तत्र न कर्तव्यं हन्यात्पूर्वापकारिणम् ॥५२॥
verses.english: The king should never allow his enemy to escape even if he bewails piteously. He should never be moved by these; on the other hand, he should destroy the person who has done him an injury.

verses.sanskrit: संग्रहानुग्रहे यत्नः सदा कार्योऽनसूयता । निग्रहश्चापि यत्नेन कर्तव्यो भूतिमिच्छता ॥५३॥
verses.english: A king seeking prosperity should studiously win over as many men as he can, and do them good. In his conduct towards his subjects he should always be shorn of malice. He should also studiously punish and restrain the wicked and disaffected.

verses.sanskrit: प्रहरिष्यन् प्रियं ब्रूयात् प्रहृत्यैव प्रियोत्तरम् । असिनापि शिरश्छित्त्वा शोचेत च रुदेत च ॥५४॥
verses.english: When he wishes to take wealth, he should say what is agreeable. Having collected wealth, he should say similar things. Having severed one's head with his sword, he should grieve and shed tears.

verses.sanskrit: निमन्त्रयीत सान्त्वेन सम्मानेन तितिक्षया । लोकाराधनमित्येतत्कर्तव्यं भूतिमिच्छता ॥५५॥
verses.english: A king seeking posperity should win over others by sweet words, honours, and gifts. Thus should he take men into his service.

verses.sanskrit: न शुष्कवैरं कुर्वीत बाहुभ्यां न नदीं तरेत् । अनर्थकमनायुष्यं गोविषाणस्य भक्षणम् । दन्ताश्च परिमृज्यन्ते रसश्चापि न लभ्यते ॥५६॥
verses.english: The king should never engage in idle disputes. He should never cross a river with the help only of his two arms. To eat cow-horns is useless and never gives strength. By eating them one's teeth are broken while the taste is not gratified.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिवर्गस्त्रिविधा पीडानुबन्धास्तथैव च । अनुबन्धं तथा ज्ञात्वा पीडां च परिवर्जयेत् ॥५७॥
verses.english: The three-fold objects have triple disadvantageous adjuncts. Carefully considering them, the disadvantages should be avoided.

verses.sanskrit: ऋणशेषमाग्निशेषं शत्रुशेषं तथैव च । पुनः पुनः प्रवर्धन्ते तस्माच्छेषं न धारयेत् ॥५८॥
verses.english: The unpaid residue of a debt, the unquenched remnant of a fire, and the unkilled remnant of foes, by and by grow and increase. Therefore, all those should be completely rooted out.

verses.sanskrit: वर्धमानमृणं तिष्ठेत्परिभूताश्च शत्रवः । जनयन्ति भयं तीव्रं व्याधयश्चाप्युपेक्षिताः ॥५९॥
verses.english: Debt which always multiplies is sure to remain unless it is wholly paid up. Likewise are the defeated foes and neglected diseases. These always create great fear.

verses.sanskrit: नासम्यक्कृतकारी स्यादप्रमत्तः सदा भवेत् । कण्टकोऽपि हि दुश्छिन्नो विकारं कुरुते चिरम् ॥६०॥
verses.english: Every work should be done completely. One should be always careful. If extracted badly, such a minute thing as a thorn leads to obstinate gangrene.

verses.sanskrit: वधेन च मनुष्याणां मार्गाणां दूषणेन च । अगाराणां विनाशैश्च परराष्ट्रं विनाशयेत् ॥६१॥
verses.english: By killing its inhabitants, by breaking its roads and otherwise injuring them, and by burning and pulling down its houses, a king should devastate an enemy's realm.

verses.sanskrit: गृध्रदृष्टिर्बकालीनः श्वचेष्टः सिंहविक्रमः । अनुद्विग्नः काकशङ्की भुजङ्गचरितं चरेत् ॥६२॥
verses.english: A king should be far-sighted like the vulture, stable like a crane, watchful like a dog, brave like a lion, dreadful like a crow, and enter into the kingdom of his enemies like a snake with ease and without anxiety.

verses.sanskrit: शूरमञ्जलिपातेन भीरुं भेदेन भेदयेत् । लुब्धमर्थप्रदानेन समं तुल्येन विग्रहः ॥६३॥
verses.english: A king should win over a hero by clasping his hands, a coward by terrorising him, and a covetous man by presents of money, and with an equal he should wage war carefully.

verses.sanskrit: श्रेणीमुख्योपजायेषु वल्लभानुनयेषु च । अमात्यान् परिरक्षेत भेदसंघातयोरपि ॥६४॥
verses.english: He should take care to create dissension among the leaders of sects and of conciliating those that are dear to him. He should protect his ministers from dissension and destruction,

verses.sanskrit: मृदुरित्यवजानन्ति तीक्ष्ण इत्युद्विजन्ति च । तीक्ष्णकाले भवेत्तीक्ष्णो मृदुकाले मृदुर्भवेत् ॥६५॥
verses.english: If the king becomes mild, the people disrespect him. If he becomes stern, the people afflicted. The rule is that he should be stern when sternness is necessary, and mild when mildness is necessary.

verses.sanskrit: मृदुनैव मृदुं छिन्दि मृदुना हन्ति दारुणम् । नासाध्यं मृदुना किंचित्तस्मात्तीक्ष्णतरो मृदुः ॥६६॥
verses.english: By mildness the mild should be conquered. By mildness one may destroy that which is dreadful. There is nothing which mildness cannot do. Therefore, mildness is said to be sharper than fierceness.

verses.sanskrit: काले मृदुर्यो भवति काले भवति दारुणः । प्रसाधयति कृत्यानि शत्रुं चाप्यधितिष्ठति ॥६७॥
verses.english: That king who becomes mild when mildness is necessary and who becomes stern when sternness is necessary, gains all his ends, and represses his enemies.

verses.sanskrit: पण्डितेन विरुद्धः सन् दूरस्थोऽस्मीति नाश्वसेत् । दीर्घौ बुद्धिमतो बाहू याभ्यां हिंसति हिंसितः ॥६८॥
verses.english: Having created an enemy in a person endued with knowledge and wisdom, one should not be satisfied with the belief that he is at a distance from his foe. The arms of an intelligent man are extensive by which he injures when injured.

verses.sanskrit: न तत्तरेद्यस्य न पारमुत्तरेन्नतद्धरेद्यत्पुनराहरेत्परः । न तत्खनेद्यस्य न मूलमुद्धरेन्न तं हन्याद्यस्य शिरो न पातयेत् ॥६९॥
verses.english: The uncrossable should not be sought to be crossed. That which the enemy would be able to recover should not be snatched from him. One should not try to dig at all if by digging one could get at the root of the thing for which one digs. One should never strike him whose head one would not cut off.

verses.sanskrit: इतीदमुक्तं वृजिनाभिसंहितं न चैतदेवं पुरुषः समाचरेत् । परप्रयुक्ते न कथं विभावयेदतो मयोक्तं भवतो हितार्थिना ॥७०॥
verses.english: A king should not always act in this way. The course of conduct that I have pointed out should be followed only in times of distress. Actuated with the desire of doing you good I have said this for instructing you as to how you should act when attacked by enemies.

verses.sanskrit: यथावदुक्तं वचनं हितार्थिना निशम्य विप्रेण सुवीरराष्ट्रपः । तथाऽकरोद्वाक्यमदीनचेतनः श्रियं च दीप्तां बुभुजे स बान्धवः ॥७१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Hearing these words given vent to by that Brahmana with the desires of doing him good, the king of Sauviras obeyed those instructions gladly and attained with his kinsmen and friends shining prosperity.
